text:
alice: noticing a weird divergence in prefix cache hit rates across deploy types after last week's kernel heuristics change. Hosted hit-rate dropped ~35% on certain prompt shapes, Dedicated/Private are mostly stable.
raj: can you paste the numbers? which workloads?
alice: quick grab from yesterday's production telemetry (30m sample):
- Hosted: overall KV hit 43% (prev ~78%) on 4k-context convo flows
- Dedicated: 74% (prev 76%)
- Private (VPC): 72% but first-token latency +12ms
seems specific to prompts with variable system+instruction prefixes and long reuse patterns.
megan: who landed the kernel/batching tweak? thought that only affected scheduling but maybe key normalization got touched.
tom: I pushed a batching heuristic tweak (pack-by-length) + small change to cache key serialization to canonicalize tensors. The serialization change was a micro-optimization: switched from msgpack -> compact-json to reduce write size for network store.
lucy: ah — Private uses a translation layer that expects msgpack keys (we still do a small adapter) whereas Hosted/Dedicated go direct to netstore. Could be a subtle canonicalization mismatch.
alice: repro steps I used in staging (quick):
- run ./tools/prefetch_probe --model llama-4x --seq 4096 --patterns sample_prompts.json --mode streaming
- compare netstore put/get latency + key length distribution
example keys shown in logs: 
```
prefix_key v1|sha256:4b3f...|len=1024|format=json
prefix_key v1|sha256:4b3f...|len=1024|format=msgpack
```
notice the format suffix differs depending on node config.
raj: that could explain misses — key namespace diverged. But why would Hosted drop so much while Dedicated stayed fine?
megan: Dedicated's netstore is colocated with runtime and we still negotiate msgpack fallback. Hosted's CDN+proxy path normalizes small keys differently and the compact-json path produces slightly different ordering for metadata fields.
alice: also saw correlation with kernel selection: when runtime picks the fused attention kernel (fast path) we see fewer cache hits vs the non-fused path. hypothesis: fused path uses in-memory normalization (trims trailing zeros) before keying to optimize memory, while non-fused leaves original bytes -> different keys.
tom: wow. The normalization was meant to be transparent but I must've only applied it in the fused branch. That's on me — will revert the normalization until we standardize keying.
lucy: for Private VPC there's another layer: an LRU gateway that rewrites keys to include node-region; if the serialization changed ordering, gateway miss rate spikes.
sre-ops: infra-bot ran a quick diff of key prefixes across environments: posted results to logs-s3: s3://redwood-prod-telemetry/kv_key_diff/1945678901.diff (short). Summary: 12% of keys had field-order differences, 7% had different suffix encoding.
megan: we should: 
1) revert the serialization change in the fused path (hotfix)
2) add unit test that verifies canonical key equality across kernels/serialization backends
3) run a targeted rewarm for Hosted (sampling-guided prefetch)
4) audit gateway rewrite logic in Private adapter for format assumptions.
alice: agree. also propose a probing job to estimate warmup ROI per-prefix shape. simple script below: 
```
# probe warmup ROI
for p in prefixes.json; do
  baseline=get_hit_rate($p)
  prefetch(prefetch_set($p))
  after=get_hit_rate($p)
  echo "$p baseline:$baseline after:$after"
done
```
we need to pick top 100 prefixes by qps.
raj: I'll open a PR for the revert and the canonical-key tests. tagging @tom @megan.
megan: after revert we should run a short canary on Hosted (2 pods) and measure delta. If hit-rate returns, schedule a rolling update.
lucy: note that Private customers might still be impacted because they cache different key form; recommend a small migration job that maps old->new keys for netstore in private deployments (run as offline batch).
infra-bot: scheduled job created: probe-prefetch-rewarm-1945678901 (ETA ~45m) :gear: logs to /var/logs/infra/probe-prefetch-rewarm-1945678901.log
sre-ops: assigned incident ticket INF-2025-239 to eng-runtime with high priority.
alice: thanks. next steps: revert + tests (raj), canary (megan), migration plan for Private (lucy). I'll collect telemetry and report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
raj: PR opened -> https://git.internal.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/2938 (revert + tests)
megan: canary started, will post numbers in ~30m
alice: posted a short perf snapshot to thread: trace ids 0x7f12,0x7f13 for follow-up profiling.
lucy: adding migration checklist to the private-deploy runbook.
sre-ops: marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if canary fails.
